cultural.vision_reason: This is a lei-like ornament made of olonā cord and ʻieʻie basketry discs, with pearl-shell and remnants of feather bundles (ʻōʻō/ʻiʻiwi feathers), materials and techniques documented as Native Hawaiian featherwork/ornament construction.

physical.title: ornament (?); religious/ritual equipment (?)
physical.summary:
Composite piece, made of a thick fibre cord (olonā) to which are attached five circular elements of basketry, made of the arial roots of the ʻieʻie plant (Freycinetia Arborea).
The basketry elements are circular in shape and brown in colour. Each is made with short pieces of ʻieʻie expanding from the centre, and connected with additional ʻieʻie pieces woven in a circular pattern. Four of the five discs show remains of small feather bundles, and seem to have been de-feathered. The feather bundles (possibly of 'ōʻō and iʻiwi), are secured with thin twisted fibre strings (possibly olonā and/or coconut). They do not cover the centre of each piece, nor do they expand to the very edge of the discs. The fifth disc is still partly feathered, and has a strand of yellow feathers (ʻōʻō) attached along the edge, and bundles of black feathers (ʻōʻō) in a circular pattern around the centre. Two of the five basketry elements are ornated with a pearl shell disc, kept in place at their centres with a peg carved of dark-brown/black wood.
The fibre cord connecting the basketry elements is plaited, and with a loop finishing each extremity. A short piece of twisted fibre string is loosely attached to one tip. The thick plaited cord is attached to the back of each basketry element with additional twisted fibre string (olonā), using two to five connecting points. One of the five elements (the feathered disc) is attached with a different mechanism: the thick plaited cord runs through the basketry work at the back, and is further secured at one other point with thin twisted fibre string.
